summary: Palmo Kyi is a Tibetologist who studied under supervisor Per Kværne (attested 2012) and teachers Hanna Havnevik and Rinzin Thargyal.

Pamela D. Winfield works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She held a post at Temple University (attested 2001) and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Elon University (attested 2015–2017).

Pamela Gutman (1944–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied at the University of Vienna and was a research student at the Australian National University circa 1972–1976.

Pandurang Vaman Kane (1880–1972) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Wilson College, Mumbai, and the University of Mumbai. He taught at Elphinstone High School, Elphinstone College, Wilson College, and Government Law College, later serving as Mumbai's vice-chancellor (1947–1949).

Paolo Visigalli is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Padua, Sapienza University of Rome, and the University of Cambridge. He held posts at NYU Shanghai (~2017–2021) and Shanghai Normal University (Professor, ~2021).

Paride Stortini is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. Attested in 2026, he was a doctoral student at the University of Chicago and a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University.

Parimal G. Patil works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1993–1996) and the University of Chicago (~1996–2002), and became a professor at Harvard University circa 2003.

Parul Dave-Mukherji specializes in Indology. She completed a DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1988–1991) and was attested in 2020 as professor of Visual Studies and Art History at Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Pascale Haag (born 1965) specializes in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat (~1996–2002) and Paris Nanterre University under Marie-Claire Gay (~2014–2018), joining the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences around 2004.
Pascale Hugon is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Pataraporn Sirikanchana is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She earned a Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania and served as a professor at Thammasat University (attested 2012).
Patrice Ladwig is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He has held posts at the University of Bristol and at the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology (attested 2012).

Patricia Berger is a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned a Ph.D. at UC Berkeley. She served as Curator at the Asian Art Museum and became Professor Emerita at UC Berkeley and the Numata Center.

Patricia Buckley Ebrey (born 1947) is a historian and Sinologist. Educated at the University of Chicago and Columbia University, she held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, the Institute for Advanced Study, and the University of Washington (1997–2020).

Patricia Fister (born 1953) is a Japanologist and historian who earned her Ph.D. at the University of Kansas. She taught at Kansas and Hakuho Women's College, and served as professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2007–2019).

Patricia Murrieta-Flores is a historian who studied at the National School of Anthropology and History and the University of Southampton. She held a post at the University of Chester (2016) before becoming Professor in Digital Humanities at Lancaster University (~2017).

Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani specializes in Sinology and Tibetology. She completed graduate study at Peking University (1990–1994) under Zumo Zhao, Zhuhong Zhang, and Shufen Mu, and earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Perry Link.

Patrick McAllister (born 1979) is an Indologist and philosopher. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (~2005–2011) and held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (~2012).

Patrick Olivelle (born 1942) is an Indologist who studied at Oxford and Pennsylvania. He held posts at Indiana University (1974–1991) and served as Chair of the Department of Asian Studies at the University of Texas at Austin from 1991.

Patrick Pranke works in Buddhist studies, history, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2004) under the supervision of Luis O. Gómez and Victor B. Lieberman.
